title: Meeting Rooms II
prompt:
The school runs tutoring sessions, each as [start, end] in minutes. Every session needs its own room while it runs. What is the minimum number of rooms needed so no two sessions share a room at the same time?

A session ending at 10 and another starting at 10 can use the same room (the first one has left).

Write minMeetingRooms(intervals).

  • minMeetingRooms([[0, 30], [5, 10], [15, 20]]) returns 2
  • minMeetingRooms([[7, 10], [2, 4]]) returns 1
  • minMeetingRooms([[1, 5], [5, 10]]) returns 1
  • minMeetingRooms([]) returns 0

Constraints: 0 to 104 sessions; 0 <= start < end. Target: O(n log n).

tests.name: back-to-back sessions share a room
tests.code: assertEqual(minMeetingRooms([[1, 5], [5, 10], [10, 15]]), 1, 'a session ending at 5 frees the room for one starting at 5');

tests.name: rooms are reused after the peak

hints: Trigger: "minimum number of rooms / platforms / servers" for intervals = the most intervals running at the same moment. Sort, then sweep through time.

Pull out the start times and the end times into two separately sorted arrays. Walk the starts in order. Before counting a new start, release every session whose end is <= this start. Track the peak of rooms in use.

Shape:

for (let i = 0; i < starts.length; i++) {
  while (endIndex < ends.length && ends[endIndex] <= starts[i]) { roomsInUse--; endIndex++; }
  roomsInUse++;
  maxRooms = Math.max(maxRooms, roomsInUse);
}

(A min-heap of end times works too: you will meet heaps in a later lesson.)
explain:
Time O(n log n) for the two sorts; the sweep is O(n) because endIndex only moves forward. Space O(n) for the two arrays. The brute force (for every minute, count the sessions covering it) depends on how long the day is, not on n.

Say it: "The answer is the maximum overlap. I'll sort starts and ends separately and sweep: each start takes a room, each end at or before that start gives one back, and I track the peak. O(n log n)." The same sweep answers "peak concurrent users" or "max servers needed" in real capacity planning.
